hero.title: Where UNDP made a difference in 2025
hero.intro: In 2025, Chad continued to strengthen its institutions and advance its development priorities, marking a new chapter for the country. Throughout the year, we worked with the Government, communities and development partners to strengthen institutions and improve the lives of the country's most vulnerable people.

paragraphs: In 2025, Chad continued to strengthen its institutions and advance its development priorities, marking a new chapter for the country.
Throughout the year, we worked with the Government, communities and development partners to **strengthen institutions** and **improve the lives of the country's most vulnerable people**.

impact.context: Between 2024 and 2025, Chad continued to face persistent economic, social, climate and institutional challenges, against a backdrop of rapid population growth and significant demand for basic services. At the same time, the country holds considerable potential, driven by a predominantly young population and opportunities for structural transformation still to be realized.
impact.lead: Chad's future is shaped by both immense potential and significant challenges.
cues: persistent economic, social, climate and institutional challenges

impact.transition: Working alongside the Government, local authorities, communities and development partners, **we delivered results that are improving people's lives across Chad.**

chapters.title: Building trust in institutions
chapters.intro: We supported more transparent, inclusive and accountable institutions through digital transformation, decentralization and greater participation in public life.

blocks.heading: Strengthening transparency and public accountability
blocks.body:
A new **national digital platform** supports more effective monitoring of government performance, enabling better-informed decision-making.

Legal and regulatory texts dating back to 1954 are now publicly accessible through the **Official Gazette digital platform**.

photos.alt: A woman in a yellow headscarf takes notes during an institutional meeting.

blocks.heading: Local governments growing into drivers of development
blocks.body:
A National Seminar on Decentralization, chaired by the President of the Republic, brought together **more than 300 stakeholders.**

**10-year National Decentralization Roadmap** adopted and disseminated nationwide.

A **shared national framework** is now helping place local governments at the heart of development.

body: For the first time, Government performance is monitored through a structured digital system, enabling more informed decision-making through real-time data.

This is made possible through a digital platform managed by the General Secretariat of the Government that centralizes performance data and supports evidence-based decision-making at the highest level.
Citizens and public institutions can now access Chad's Official Gazette and legal texts dating back to 1954 through a dedicated digital platform.

figures.label: official documents digitized and publicly accessible
years of institutional memory now accessible through the Official Gazette digital platform

body: The legislative and local elections held in December 2024 marked Chad's return to constitutional order and resulted in a significant increase in women's representation across elected institutions.
We supported national and local institutions in promoting the rights of persons with disabilities.
In Hadjer Lamis, 100 persons with disabilities received mobility aids, including wheelchairs and walking canes, helping them regain mobility, independence and dignity.

Mobile court hearings reduced prison overcrowding by 10% and enabled 956 detainees – including women and minors – to receive legal aid. Four correctional facilities were equipped with new water infrastructure, improving hygiene, health and overall detention conditions.

Health facilities were strengthened through the provision of medical equipment, cold chain systems and solar energy solutions, helping improve the quality and continuity of essential health services, particularly in underserved areas.
health-2.figureLabel: biomedical technicians were also trained to operate and maintain the equipment, strengthening local capacity, promoting long-term sustainability and fostering national ownership.

body: Through an intensive one-month AI bootcamp in Guinea and a specialized cybersecurity programme in Senegal, young Chadians strengthened practical digital skills alongside peers from across Francophone Africa, helping prepare a new generation of digital innovators.

body: Behind every result in this report are strong partnerships, shared commitment and collective action. Working hand in hand with the Government and a wide range of bilateral and multilateral partners, UNDP is helping expand opportunities, reach the most vulnerable communities and advance sustainable development across Chad.

**Our partners include:** the African Development Bank, the European Union, France, the Global Environment Facility, the Global Fund, Germany, the Islamic Development Bank, Japan, the Netherlands, Slovenia, Sweden, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, the UN Peacebuilding Fund, the UNDP Funding Windows and the World Bank.
